subject: Quick demo + traffic snapshot from BrightLane AI
messages:
From: Chris Lee <chris@brightlane.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Demo request — BrightLane trial + quick traffic note

Hi Priyom,

I signed up for the self-serve trial this morning and wanted to request a short walkthrough/demo to make sure we configure things right. We're evaluating Redwood to power two features in our product: (1) agent-assisted customer support summarization, and (2) semantic search for internal knowledge.

A few quick pieces of context:
- Expected monthly inference volume (stage 1 pilot): ~1,000,000 generation/embedding ops per month
- Typical tokens per generation request: ~600–900 (median ~750)
- Peak concurrent requests we expect: ~40–60 (US east traffic pattern)
- Desired timeline: pilot in June, production Q3 if things go well

I've attached a small traffic snapshot (traffic_snapshot.csv) with sample request histograms and a one-pager. We'd like to cover: ingestion, latency SLOs, cost per token estimates, and what a quick pilot looks like. 30 minutes would be ideal.

Available windows (ET) next week:
- Tue 5/18: 10:00–11:00 or 15:00–16:00
- Wed 5/19: 09:00–11:30
- Thu 5/20: 14:00–16:00

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation.

Regards,
Chris Lee
VP Product, BrightLane AI
chris@brightlane.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: traffic_snapshot.csv, promo_onepager.pdf

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Chris Lee <chris@brightlane.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:38:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — BrightLane trial + quick traffic note

Hi Chris — thanks for the signup and the snapshot, this is helpful. Happy to run a focused 30-minute session. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock a slot so the demo time focuses on what matters for your pilot: 

1) Use case prioritization — will the initial pilot prioritize generation (summaries/chat) or embeddings/search? If both, which is the primary SLO?
2) Latency & SLA — are you targeting p95 < 500ms for small queries, or is higher latency acceptable if cost is lower?
3) Data residency / compliance — any requirement for EU data residency or SOC2/Papertrail for logs during pilot?
4) Model preferences — planning to use open models only or interested in Redwood-managed variants / quantized options?
5) Integration — do you expect server-side API calls from a backend (typical) or client-side calls from apps?

If you can answer those quickly I will: (a) confirm the best slot, (b) include Monica (solutions engineer) to prep a tailored runbook, and (c) prepare a quick cost sketch for the volumes you sent.

Proposed slots (ET): Tue 5/18 15:00, Wed 5/19 10:00, Thu 5/20 14:30. Let me know which works and I will send an invite.

Best,

—
Priyom Das
Enterprise SDR, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

(On a related note: Monica, can you pull a quick pilot sketch for 1M ops/month with token median 750 and include a small concurrency recommendation?)

From: Chris Lee <chris@brightlane.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: BrightLane AI <sales@brightlane.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — BrightLane trial + quick traffic note

Thanks Priyom — answers inline: 

> 1) Use case prioritization — will the initial pilot prioritize generation (summaries/chat) or embeddings/search?
We're prioritizing embeddings/search first (we want solid semantic similarity for internal KB), but we will also validate generation for support summarization (secondary).

> 2) Latency & SLA — are you targeting p95 < 500ms for small queries, or is higher latency acceptable if cost is lower?
Ideally p95 < 400–500ms for search queries. For generation (async summaries) we can accept higher tail latency (~1.5s).

> 3) Data residency / compliance — any requirement for EU data residency or SOC2/Papertrail for logs during pilot?
No EU residency requirement for now. SOC2 compliance is a must for our vendor evaluation, but we can start the pilot while you provide SOC2 documentation.

> 4) Model preferences — planning to use open models only or interested in Redwood-managed variants / quantized options?
Open models to start; interested in quantized variants if they maintain the quality of embeddings.

> 5) Integration — do you expect server-side API calls from a backend (typical) or client-side calls from apps?
All server-side/backend calls.

Slot update: Wed 5/19 10:00 ET works best for us. If it helps, please send a calendar invite — I'll forward internally.

—
Chris

Subject: Re: Demo request — BrightLane trial + quick traffic note

Perfect — Wed 5/19 10:00 ET is locked. I sent a calendar invite (Zoom link + agenda). Monica, thanks for the quick pilot sketch — attaching the one-pager and our suggested pilot runbook in the invite.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: intros + success criteria for pilot
- 10m: architecture + integration path (server-side ingestion, tokens/throughput)
- 10m: pilot economics & recommended configuration (batching, quantization, concurrency)
- 5m: next steps (access, trial keys, evaluation metric)

Next steps for us:
- Monica to produce a short cost sketch (1M ops/month, median token 750) and a concurrency/instance recommendation by Monday 5/17.
- Chris to confirm internal attendees and any security contacts who should receive SOC2 docs.

See you Wed — invite from priyom_das@redwood.com with Zoom link.

Best,
Priyom
